newsitem.title: UK: HRT does not increase cervical cancer risk - study.
newsitem.headline: HRT does not increase cervical cancer risk - study.

text.p: Italian researchers reported on Friday they had found no evidence that hormone replacement therapy (HRT) increases the risk of cervical cancer.
Fabio Parazzini and colleagues at the Institute of Pharmacological Research in Milan said their study of 645 women indicated that HRT may even protect against cervical cancer.
"The protection tended to be somewhat stronger for women reporting first oestrogen use before age 50," they wrote in a report in the British Medical Journal.
"The odds of cervical cancer decreased with duration of use," they added. "The reduced risk seems to persist for 10 years or more."
There is clear evidence that HRT helps prevents osteoporosis, the weakening of the bones that often comes with age.

It also greatly diminishes some of the worst symptoms of the menopause such as mood swings, hot flushes and, more seriously, the increasing tendency for women to show "male" patterns of sickness such as higher rates of heart disease.
However, an increase in blood clots and endometrial cancer -- cancer of the lining of the uterus -- may come with HRT.
Other studies have indicated that taking hormones such as those in birth control pills can increase the risk of cervical cancer.
But there has been little examination of the effects of HRT, which replaces oestrogen without adding other female hormones such as progesterone, on cervical cancer.
